mcqs.question: What is the main purpose of science?

options.B: To understand the natural world through observation and evidence

mcqs.answer: To understand the natural world through observation and evidence
mcqs.explanation: Science aims to explain how the natural world works by using systematic observation, evidence and logical reasoning. Options A, C and D describe activities that are not the core purpose of scientific inquiry.

mcqs.learning_point: Curiosity as the starting point of scientific investigation
mcqs.question: Which of the following best describes the role of curiosity in scientific investigations?

options.A: Curiosity is irrelevant; only data matters
options.B: Curiosity sparks the initial question that leads to investigation
options.C: Curiosity replaces the need for experiments

mcqs.answer: Curiosity sparks the initial question that leads to investigation
mcqs.explanation: Scientific work begins when curiosity makes us ask a question about something we observe. The other options misstate the function of curiosity in the scientific process.

mcqs.question: In scientific inquiry, what is the difference between observation and careful description?

options.A: Observation is guessing; description is writing
options.B: Observation is noticing a phenomenon; careful description records details accurately
options.C: Observation uses math; description uses art
options.D: Observation is done after experiments; description before

mcqs.answer: Observation is noticing a phenomenon; careful description records details accurately
mcqs.explanation: Observation means detecting something with the senses or tools. A careful description follows, noting size, shape, color, etc., so others can understand exactly what was seen. The other choices mix unrelated activities.

mcqs.question: A student notices that a plant grows faster in sunlight than in shade. Which question should the student ask next?

options.A: Why does the plant need water?
options.B: How does sunlight affect the plant’s growth?
options.D: How many leaves does the plant have?

mcqs.answer: How does sunlight affect the plant’s growth?
mcqs.explanation: The observation concerns light, so the logical next question probes the relationship between sunlight and growth. Options A, C, and D are unrelated to the observed difference.

mcqs.question: If a metal rod is heated, it expands. Which prediction follows this observation?

options.A: The rod will shrink when cooled

mcqs.answer: The rod will shrink when cooled
mcqs.explanation: From the observation that heating makes the rod expand, a reasonable prediction is that cooling will cause it to contract. The other options are not logical consequences of thermal expansion.

mcqs.question: Sam thinks that adding sugar makes tea taste sweeter. To test this, he prepares two cups, one with sugar and one without, and asks friends to rate sweetness. Which part of the scientific process is Sam using?
mcqs.explanation: Sam is performing an experiment to gather data that will support or refute his idea. Formulating a hypothesis (A) occurs before the test, while drawing conclusions (C) and communicating results (D) happen after evidence is collected.

mcqs.learning_point: Drawing conclusions from observations and evidence
mcqs.question: A child observes that all swans they have seen are white and concludes that all swans are white. What is the flaw in this conclusion?

options.A: The child used too many examples
options.B: The child ignored other possible evidence

mcqs.answer: The child ignored other possible evidence
mcqs.explanation: Concluding that all swans are white based only on limited observations ignores the possibility of other swan colors that the child hasn't seen. Scientific conclusions require broader evidence. Options A, C, and D do not describe the error.

mcqs.learning_point: Revising explanations when evidence requires it
mcqs.question: During an experiment, Maya predicts that a magnet will attract a plastic rod. The rod does not move. Which reasoning best explains what Maya should do next?

options.A: Keep the same explanation because predictions are always right
options.B: Revise her explanation to state that magnets attract only certain materials
options.C: Discard the experiment as a failure
options.D: Change the magnet to a stronger one without reconsidering the explanation

mcqs.answer: Revise her explanation to state that magnets attract only certain materials
mcqs.explanation: When evidence contradicts a prediction, scientists modify their explanations. Maya should note that magnets attract ferromagnetic materials, not plastic. Options A and C ignore the evidence, and D changes a variable without addressing the conceptual error.
